examples.en: My dad is a role model for me.
The doctor took a blood sample.
The rug has a nice pattern.

related.en: role model, example to follow — what people look up to
sample, specimen — taken for testing: blood, fabric
pattern, design — on fabric, on a rug

examples.en: I'm going home, I'm tired.
I was at home all day today.

related.en: home (to) — answers «where to?»: идем кући, враћам се кући
at home — answers «where?»: сам сам код куће, остајем код куће

note: Unlike English «home», «кући» is only for going: say «код куће сам», not «кући сам».

examples.en: In the evening I watch TV.
The TV set is by the window.

related.en: TV set (the device) — the object itself: укључи телевизор
television, TV (broadcasting) — what you watch: на телевизији дају филм

examples.en: Fry the eggs in the frying pan.
The pie is baked in a large baking pan.
Milk is heated in a saucepan.
Soup is cooked in a large pot.

related.en: frying pan, skillet — for frying eggs, meat, pancakes
frying pan, baking tray — for frying or baking in the oven
saucepan (smallish) — for boiling pasta, sauce, milk
large pot, cooking pot — soup, sarma; земљани лонац - clay pot

note: Ло̀нац is usually bigger than a шерпа.

meanings: who is who in renting: власник, закуподавац, закупац, станар

examples.en: The owner of the apartment lives abroad.
The landlord is asking for a two-month deposit.

examples.sr: Нови [за̀купац] плаћа кирију првог у месецу.
examples.en: The new tenant pays the rent on the first of every month.
All the residents of the building are at the meeting.

related.en: owner — the person the property belongs to
landlord, lessor — rents out the property; not necessarily the owner
tenant, lessee — rents the property under a contract
resident — whoever lives in the building or apartment

note: Ста̀на̄р is the more general word: it covers a tenant and an owner who lives in the apartment.

meanings: игла, чиода, шпенадла, дупла игла: which needle or pin

examples.en: Thread the needle.
Pin the fabric before sewing.

examples.sr: Пази, испала ти је [шпена̀дла] на тепих.
examples.en: Careful, your pin fell on the carpet.

examples.sr: Имаш ли једну [ду̏плу и̏глу]? Пукло ми је дугме.
examples.en: Do you have a safety pin? My button came off.

related.en: sewing needle — with an eye for the thread
pin (tailor's) — the standard and most common word
pin — the same, colloquial; from German, more common in Vojvodina and among older people
safety pin — a clasp that holds fabric together

note: A safety pin is «дупла игла», literally «double needle».

meanings: и, а, те, па: how to join parts of a sentence

examples.sr: Он долази данас, [и] она долази данас.
examples.en: He's coming today, and she's coming today.

examples.sr: Он долази данас, [а] она долази сутра.
examples.en: He's coming today, but she's coming tomorrow.

examples.sr: Купићу јабуке и крушке, [те] хлеб и пециво.
examples.en: I'll buy apples and pears, plus bread and pastries.

examples.sr: Нестало им је новца, [па] су се вратили кући.
examples.en: They ran out of money, so they went back home.

related.en: and, but — stresses a difference, a contrast
and also, plus — adds to a list; sounds more bookish
and so, and then — the next step or a consequence

note: At the start of a reply, «па» also means «well, okay»: па до̀бро.

meanings: клопати, папати, шопати, хасати, њопати, ручкати: slang for eating

examples.sr: Хеј, шта радиш? - Ево [кло̏пам], завршавам за петнаест минута.
examples.en: Hey, what are you doing? - Just eating, I'll be done in fifteen minutes.

examples.sr: Мама, хоћу нешто да [па̏пам]. Је ли готов ручак?
examples.en: Mom, I want something to eat. Is lunch ready?

examples.sr: Полако, брате, [шо̏паш] тај хамбургер као да је последњи на свету.
examples.en: Slow down, man, you're wolfing down that hamburger like it's the last one on earth.

examples.sr: Милоше, хоћеш ли да [ха̏само] нешто? Има добрих пљескавица овде близу.
examples.en: Miloš, do you want to grab a bite? There are some good pljeskavicas near here.
The kids were scarfing down chocolate all afternoon.
Let's have lunch at my place.

related.en: to chow down, to scoff — the most common colloquial verb
to eat, to have a bite — homey
to wolf down — to eat greedily and fast, without a break
to grab a bite, to eat together
to scarf down — to eat without restraint

note: The neutral verb is је̏сти. All of these are colloquial and out of place in formal speech.

meanings: станица, стајалиште, перон, колосек: station and stop

examples.en: The bus station is next to the railway station.
I'll wait for you at the stop in front of the school.

examples.sr: Кад изађеш из воза, наћи ћемо се на [пѐрону].
examples.en: When you get off the train, we'll meet on the platform.
The train leaves from track two.

related.en: stop (public transport) — a pole with a timetable; in speech often also «станица»
platform — where people wait for the train
track — departures are announced by track number

note: Ста̀ница also appears in other phrases: полицијска станица - police station.

skip: false-friend article: these Serbian words look like Russian ones but mean something else; no such confusion for English speakers

examples.sr: Књига кошта осамсто динара, а [поштарѝна] је још триста.
examples.en: The book costs eight hundred dinars, and postage is another three hundred.

examples.sr: Курир тражи [о̏ткупнину] од четири хиљаде петсто динара.
examples.en: The courier asks for four thousand five hundred dinars cash on delivery.

related.en: cash on delivery amount — what you pay the courier on receipt
postage, shipping cost — what it costs to send a parcel

note: Откупнѝна covers the price of the goods plus the поштарина, if the seller did not pay for delivery.

examples.sr: Можете ли да [прецизѝрате] рок за плаћање?
examples.en: Can you specify the payment deadline?

examples.sr: Молим вас, [поја̀сните] шта сте имали у виду.
examples.en: Please clarify what you meant.

examples.sr: Можете ли да ми [о̀бјасните] ово правило?
examples.en: Can you explain this rule to me?
The commission will establish the cause of the fire.

related.en: to specify, to make more precise — a deadline, data, wording: прецизирајте захтев
to clarify — something already said but not understood
to explain — the most general word: a topic, a rule, a law
to establish, to determine (regional) — found mostly in news reports

note: If in doubt, use обја̀снити: the other three sound businesslike and bookish.

examples.en: The wind bent the antenna on the roof.

examples.sr: Девојчица је [накрѝвила] главу и насмешила се.
examples.en: The girl tilted her head and smiled.
Why did you tilt the chair?

related.en: to bend, to warp — change the shape, make uneven
to tilt to one side — накривити главу, накривити капу
to tilt, to put sideways (colloq.) — often with a joking tone

note: Искривити and накри̏вити are neutral and fine anywhere. Keep нахерити for talking with friends.

examples.en: Every day I write messages to friends.
Mom, I need to pee!

related.en: to write — пишем, пишеш: a letter, a text; past писао, писала
to pee (colloq.) — пишам, пишаш: an everyday word; past пишао, пишала

examples.sr: Узми [о̀ва̄ј] кључ, он је на столу.
examples.en: Take this key, it's on the table.
Give me that phone, please.

examples.sr: Видиш ли [о̀на̄ј] мост на крају улице?
examples.en: Do you see that bridge at the end of the street?

related.en: this — the thing right next to you, within reach
that (nearer) — a bit farther away, out of reach; also used for what was just mentioned

note: Three degrees of distance: овај - near, тај - farther, онај - far. All three change by gender and case, like adjectives.

key: cmp:изгледа да-имам утисак да-чини ми се
meanings: «чини ми се», «имам утисак да» or «изгледа да»?

examples.en: I think it's late.

examples.sr: [Ѝма̄м у̀тисак] да нас нико не слуша.
examples.en: I have the feeling nobody is listening to us.
It looks like it's going to rain.

related.en: it seems to me, I think — the usual phrase for an opinion or a guess; an impersonal verb with the dative: чини ми се, чини ти се
I have the impression that — a conclusion based on a general impression, not on facts
it looks like, it seems that — a conclusion from visible signs: «judging by everything»

note: Three ways to say «it seems». Each is followed by «да» and an ordinary clause. «Чини ми се» is a personal opinion, «изгледа да» a conclusion from signs.

examples.sr: Наш [у̀читељ] је стрпљив према малим ђацима.
examples.en: Our teacher is patient with the little kids.
The math teacher gives extra lessons.

examples.sr: Наш [про̀фесор] из гимназије и данас нас памти.
examples.en: Our teacher from high school still remembers us today.

related.en: primary school teacher — teaches small children in the first grades
subject teacher — teaches their own subject in the older grades of elementary school
secondary school teacher, university professor — what teachers in a gymnasium and high school are called, as well as university lecturers

note: The words differ by the age of the pupils. For women: учитељица, наставница, професорка.

examples.en: The kids are decorating the Christmas tree.
The neighbors are decorating their windows with little lights.

related.en: to decorate, to dress up — a tree, a table, a room for a holiday; sounds more colloquial and warm
to decorate — a neutral verb: a house, an apartment, windows, a cake; pf. украсити

note: Both mean «to decorate»: китити is used more for festive things - a Christmas tree or a table, while украшавати fits anything.

examples.en: Coffee with milk, please.
Salad with cheese is tasty.
Coffee with a cake (served separately).
We're walking along the Danube.

related.en: with, together, as part of — when something is part of the whole or someone is with you: кафа са млеком, идем са другом; са + gen. - off, from a surface
next to, along, in addition — when things are served separately, side by side, or run along: кафа уз колач, шетамо уз Дунав, плесати уз музику

note: Са - together inside or as a component (the milk is already in the coffee), уз - alongside and in addition (coffee and a cake served separately). «Кафа уз млеко» would mean coffee with a glass of milk beside it.

examples.en: Their child already goes to school.
That boy plays soccer every day.

examples.sr: Кад сам био [кли̏нац], играо сам фудбал.
examples.en: When I was a kid, I played soccer.

related.en: child — neutral, a boy or a girl
kid, lad — colloquial, of a boy or a teenager

note: «Дете» always fits, «дечак» only a boy, «клинац» is colloquial and familiar.

meanings: to look at, examine, consider: погледати, прегледати, размотрити, преиспитати

examples.en: I want to look into the distance.
We have to inspect the apartment before signing.
The committee will consider your application.
The terms of the contract need to be reconsidered.

related.en: to take a look, to glance — simply look somewhere or at something
to examine, to look over, to check — to inspect an apartment carefully or go through a document
to consider, to look into — to study an application or proposal and make a decision
to reconsider, to re-examine — to think over the terms or a decision again

meanings: how to end a letter: с поштовањем, срдачан поздрав, срдачно or поздрав?

examples.sr: Хвала на одговору. [С пошто̀вањем], Ана Јовановић
examples.en: Thank you for your reply. Sincerely, Ana Jovanović

examples.sr: Видимо се у петак. [Ср̏да̄чан по̏здра̄в], Марко
examples.en: See you on Friday. Kind regards, Marko
Thank you for your help. Warmly, Jelena
I'll be in touch tomorrow. Best, Nikola

related.en: respectfully, yours sincerely — the most formal, for officials and people you don't know
kind regards, best wishes — professional but warmer
warmly, cordially — a short warm one when you already know each other
regards, all the best — neutral and less formal, for ordinary work correspondence

note: The shorter and simpler the sign-off, the less distance: from the formal «с поштовањем» to a plain «поздрав».

examples.en: A strong wind is blowing from the river today.
The košava is blowing in Belgrade.

related.en: košava — a specific cold, gusty wind of Serbia: the Danube, Belgrade, Banat, Vojvodina

note: Every кошава is a ветар, but not every ветар is a кошава: only the local eastern wind is called that.

Many names of clothes and everyday things came into Serbian from Turkish:
• shoes and socks: папу̀че, чи̏зме, чара̀пе, па̀тике
• the rest: ма̀рама, ка̀иш, ду̀гме, џе̏п, то́рба

Knowing these words helps you recognize them in Turkish too.

There are far more Turkisms in everyday speech than clothing names.
title: Turkisms in clothing names

note:
Add «-с» to a part of the day to say «this morning», «this evening», «today»:
• ју̏тро - ју̏тро̄с
• ве̏че̄ - вечѐрас
• да̑н - да̀нас

For «last night» there is a separate word си̏но̄ћ.

The seasonal adverbs are formed the same way, usually about the season just past: зѝмӯс, про̀лето̄с, ле̏то̄с, јесѐнас.
title: Time adverbs with the suffix -с

related.en: here, kitty-kitty (what you call a cat with)

note:
Names for cats:
• ма̏чка - a cat in general, also a female
• ма́чак, ма̏чор - a tomcat
• ма̏че (n.) - a kitten, pl. мачићи
• ма́ца - affectionate

You call a cat with «мац-мац», the way English says «here, kitty-kitty».
title: What cats are called

related.en: short form of Драган or Драгана
short form of Дејан or Дејана

note:
Male names can end in -а: Нѝкола, Сѝниша, Ѝлија.

The short forms Неша, Миша, Воја, Света are male too.

Гага, Боба, Деја can be male or female: Гага - from Дра̀ган or Дра̀гана.
title: Male names ending in «-а» and short forms

related.en: nickname or short form of a name

note:
Surnames often end in -ић, less often in -ски and -ов/-ев.

На́димак is a nickname or a short form of a name: Аца, Сале, Бебан (from бе́ба).

The patronymic is the «сре̏дње и̏ме»: the father's name in parentheses between the first name and the surname. It is written only in documents.
title: First name, surname, nickname and patronymic

related.en: to turn on the string lights

note:
The tree (је̏лка) is decorated: китити јелку, качити украсе, упалити лампице.

Ornaments: куглице, шишарке, пахуљице, фигурице, гирланде, ве́нац.

Festive fun: ва̏троме̄т, петарде, пр̀скалице.

Gifts: по̀клон, пакѐтић, чѐститка, бомбо̀њера.
title: New Year vocabulary

related.en: the traditional Christmas gift-bringer, an old man

note:
In Serbia, New Year gifts have two heroes:
• Бо̀жић Ба̏та - comes on Orthodox Christmas, January 7, dressed as a priest, and stands for the old tradition
• Де̏да Мра̏з - came from the USSR, merged in people's minds with Santa, lives in Lapland and brings gifts under the tree on the night of January 1
title: Two Father Frosts

related.en: January 5, the day before Christmas Eve
oak branches burned on Christmas Eve
ceremonial loaf with a coin inside
the first guest of the holiday

note:
Days of the Serbian Christmas:
• Туциндан (January 5) - pigs are slaughtered for the holiday
• Бадњи дан (January 6) - Christmas Eve; in the evening the ба̏дња̄к is burned
• Бо̀жић (January 7) - wheat with thin green sprouts stands in the middle of the table, the чесница with a coin inside is broken, and the first guest, по̀ложајник, brings luck
title: Serbian Christmas: days and customs

note:
The Serbian for a snowman is Сне̏шко Бѐлић. A riddle about him:

Ло̀нац и̏ма, а̏ли нѝје ку̏ва̄р.
Мѐтлу и̏ма, а̏ли нѝје чѝста̄ч.
Бе̏о ма̏нтил, а̏ли нѝје лѐка̄р.

(He has a pot, but he is not a cook. He has a broom, but he is not a janitor. A white coat, but he is not a doctor.)
title: A riddle about a snowman

related.en: a mountain massif and Serbia's main ski resort

note:
Копаоник is a national park and Serbia's main ski resort.

The Romans and the Ottomans called it the «silver mountain» because of its silver mining.

The country's highest waterfall, Јеловарник, is here, along with many endemic plants. Nearby is Ђавоља варош: strange clay pillars.
title: Копаоник - a mountain and ski resort

note:
Ша̀лтер is the window in an office where documents are accepted, and шалтеруша is the employee behind it.

Папирологија is a joking name for paper bureaucracy.

The famous phrase «Фали ти један папир» (ФТЈП) means you have to bring yet another document.
title: Шалтер, шалтеруша and папирологија

related.en: «bready», the full name of the bakery

note:
In colloquial speech the initial «х» often drops, and an apostrophe takes its place:
• хле̏б - 'леб
• ха̀јде - 'а̀јде
• хла́дно - 'ладно

Hence the name of the Belgrade bakery «Лебовски», short for «Хлебовски».
title: Where the «Х» goes

examples.en: See you on Friday.
On Wednesdays I go to the pool.
What are you doing this weekend?

note:
A one-time event: «у» + accusative.
• у понѐдељак, у сре̑ду, у пе́так, у су̀боту

A regular event: the instrumental case with no preposition.
• у́то̄рком, сре́до̄м - on Tuesdays, on Wednesdays
• радним данима - on weekdays
• викендом - on weekends

The weekend breaks the first rule: one particular weekend is «за вѝкенд», not «у викенд». Шта радиш за викенд? - What are you doing this weekend?
title: Days of the week: one-time and regular events

note:
Basic words: ко̀са, фризу́ра, ши̏ша̄ње.

Types of hair: кратка, ду́га, равна, коврџава, таласаста, офарбана.

Hairstyles: паж, ши̏шке, коњски реп, пу́нђа, локне.

Verbs: ши́шати, пра̏ти, су́шити, чѐшљати, фа̑рбати, фенѝрати, ра̀внати ко̏су.
title: At the hairdresser's

related.en: you know, you know how it is

note:
In everyday speech Serbs fill pauses with words: па, зна̏чи, у ствари, да кажем, оно, е сад, ми̏слӣм, зна̑ш ка̏ко, о̀ва̄ј.

They buy time and sound natural, but don't overuse them.
title: Filler words (поштапалице)

note:
Names of the parts of speech:
• inflected: и̏меница, гла̏гол, при́дев, за̑меница
• not inflected: при́лог, пре́длог, ре̏чца, ве̑знӣк, у̏звӣк
title: Parts of speech in Serbian

related.en: kajmak, a soft creamy dairy spread

note:
The basics of a grill: пљѐскавица, ћева̀пчићи, ра̏жњићи, кобасице, пилећа крилца.

They are served with: лу̏к, шопска салата, а̀јва̄р, ка̀јмак, у̏рнебе̄с, па̀влака.

The meat is marinated and cooked over embers or on charcoal (ћу̀мур).
title: A Serbian grill menu

related.en: How many kilos do you lift?

note:
The room and equipment: терета̀на, тѐгови, собни бицикл, тра̏ка за тр̀ча̄ње, спра̏ва.

Exercises: чу̏чњеви, склѐкови, згибови, скокови, тр̏бушњаци, загре̏ва̄ње.

Phrases:
• «Колѝко јо̏ш се̑рија?»
• радити руке, радити ноге, радити трбушњаке
• «Колико килограма дижеш?»
title: At the gym

note:
Nicknames based on appearance are often formed with suffixes:
• -ко: дебе́љко, бу̏цко, мршавко, ћелавко, наочарко
• -оња: брадоња, бр́коња, ду̀гоња
• мрга

The tone is usually joking and warm.
title: Nicknames based on appearance

note:
At the beach: пла́жа, су̏нцобра̄н, лѐжа̄љка, пе́сак, шљу́нак, та̏ла̄с, о̏бала.

Things: на̏оча̄ре за су̑нце, торба за плажу, пешкир за плажу, ку̀па̄ћӣ ко̀стӣм, купаће гаће, мле́ко за су̏нча̄ње.

Activities: правити замак од песка, ро̀ње̄ње, пли̏ва̄ње, ку́пати се, су̀нчати се, поцр̀нети.
title: Beach vocabulary

note:
Names of cartoon characters in Serbian:
• Snow White - Снежана
• Sleeping Beauty - Успавана лепотица
• Bugs Bunny - Душко Дугоушко
• Donald Duck - Пајо Патак

In Croatia the characters have completely different names, so Croatian content differs noticeably in vocabulary.
title: Cartoon characters: Serbian and Croatian

related.en: the back of beyond, where there is not even a trace of a road
the boondocks, where nobody ever comes
the end of the world, the middle of nowhere

note:
Jokes about the end of the world use invented place names:
• Бестрагија - from «без тра̑га»: a place with no road
• Недођија - where nobody comes; it is also Neverland from «Peter Pan»
• Тунгузија - from the Tungus people, a symbol of wild, remote wilderness

There is also a rude expression with the root «ву̑к».
title: Made-up places in the middle of nowhere

note:
Writing in Latin letters without č, ć, š, ž, đ gives «bald Latin»: ћелава латиница or ошишана латиница.

Sometimes the meaning changes: «šarmom» (with charm) turns into «sarmom» - with sarma, the cabbage dish (са̀рма).
title: Bald Latin script

note:
Са̀станак is a meeting, including an online one. You also hear по́зив or, colloquially, кол.

The meeting:
• зака́зати са̀станак
• придружити се састанку
• напу̀стити са̀станак

Actions:
• послати позивницу, прихватити позивницу, одбити позивницу
• подесити камеру и ми̏крофо̄н
• поде́лити ѐкра̄н
• сни́мити са̀станак

Participants: у̀чеснӣк, излагач.
title: Online call

note:
Verbs:
• чи̏стити ста̑н, сређи́вати ста̑н, спре́мати ста̑н
• прати судове, пе́глати
• о̀брисати под, о̀брисати пра̀шину

note:
School uses a five-point scale:
• 5 - пѐтица, о̏дличан
• 4 - чѐтво̄рка, вр̏ло до̏бар
• 3 - тро́јка, до̏бар
• 2 - дво́јка, до̏во̄љан
• 1 - једѝница, не̏дово̄љан

At university the scale runs from 5 to 10:
• 10 - и̏зузе̄тан
• 9 - о̏дличан
• 8 - вр̏ло до̏бар
• 7 - до̏бар
• 6 - до̏во̄љан, the minimum to pass
• 5 - не̏дово̄љан, exam failed
title: School grades in Serbia

note:
A state: an adverb plus «је»: су̏нчано је, о̏блачно је, магло̀вито је.

Changes: отоплило је, захладнело је, наоблачило се, разведрава се.

Phenomena: пљу̑сак, олу́ја, не̏вре̄ме, мѐћава, ма̀гла, ду́га.

• Latin Alba Graeca
• Hungarian Nándorfehérvár
